title: Behavioural responses of overwintering herring to candidate whale deterrent signals
content:
Abstract
Whales and fisheries targeting the same resources may have unfortunate consequences. Whales may become entangled in fishing gear and injured, or the gear may be damaged, and the catch lost. Acoustic signals can be used to deter whales from such interactions. However, to be efficient, the signals should not alter the behaviour of the target species and thereby reduce the catchability for the fishery. In this study, we examined the behavioural response of overwintering Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus) in a Norwegian fjord to acoustic signals under development for use in deterring humpback and killer whales during fishing operations. The signals were of 0.2 s duration, less than 0.005 s rise time and spanned frequencies from 200 to 3200 Hz. Volume backscattering strength (SV) versus depth (z) was measured before, during and after sound transmission. Herring density, abundance, location and dispersion, as estimated by SV, did not change significantly following the transmissions. This indicates that herring did not change their spatial distribution or orientation in response to the transmissions. We therefore conclude that the signals, at the levels tested, may be used without affecting the behaviour of overwintering herring.
